method: Source literal/coordinate audit and exact scalar arithmetic; no production CAD modification, native CSG, slice, print or FEA.
coordinate_convention: Input local z; CAD Y = local z - 82, axis CAD X=75,Z=5.

current_face_stacks.part: body between outer washer and sleeve seat
current_face_stacks.description: PETG; axial thickness 6.5, central through bore D4.5

current_face_stacks.part: cover between sleeve seat and outer washer
current_face_stacks.description: PETG; axial thickness 4.5, central through bore D4.5

current_parallel_path: Cover -> two cheek-column contacts at z8 -> body. Their own M3x30 screws close these faces. Column keys top9.5 vs cover key-pocket roof9.7 leave .2 clearance and are not the axial stop.

seat_annulus.status: Most tube end rests on PETG annulus; small inner ring overhangs D4.5 through bore.

length_cases.first_contacts: Both cheek-column stop faces at z8 can close while sleeve has total .02 end gap; sleeve may float or touch either single seat.
Sleeve seats and cheek-column stop faces can nominally close simultaneously.
Rear-seated sleeve contacts cover roof .02 before cheek-column stop faces close; cover lift .02 or deformation required.

overconstraint_conclusion: No nominal geometric solid overlap at L15. However the central sleeve/seat chain and two remote column stops redundantly set the same cover separation. L variation cannot be absorbed while insisting all three stops are rigidly closed; short tube loses the central stop, long tube needs deformation or lifted columns. This does not by itself prove the lever jams.

unimplemented_through_sleeve_proposal.length_tolerance_status: Uses the same +/-0.02 only as a calculation input; no new supplier configuration verification here.
required_changes: Body and cover center bores become through D8.3; old blind seats removed.
Move rear washer to z[-13,-12.2], front washer to [14.2,15.0], screw underhead to15.0 and nut to[-16.2,-13]. Retain hardware dimensions. Old hardware positions would overlap sleeve ends by .2 each.
unimplemented_through_sleeve_proposal.metal_clamp_path: head -> front washer -> entire sleeve -> rear washer -> nut; PETG bypassed only if actual sleeve length exceeds actual closed housing outer-face span.

capture.status: Nominal positive capture, not tolerance/strength proof. Both washers/nut/head must remain; no positive antirotation to body is present.

unimplemented_through_sleeve_proposal.moving_clearance: Internal cavity and lever/thrust stack unchanged, so their nominal .5 total endplay remains. Axle-cartridge float is a separate .4 DOF and is not additional lever travel.
unimplemented_through_sleeve_proposal.housing_retention: The two side M3 screws/columns hold the cover to the body. The center fastener clamps only its own metal cartridge in this proposal; it no longer provides center PETG preload.
constraints_to_define: Treat the cartridge as deliberately floating in rotation/axial translation, or add an explicit datum/capture/antirotation scheme. It cannot be called a fixed shaft merely because its own screw is tight.
For metal-only clamping require L_min > H_outer_max including outer-face flatness/parallelism and print tolerance; the .4 nominal clearance alone does not prove this.
Confirm washer minimum OD vs maximum through-hole and eccentricity, edge bearing under axial loads, and side-M3 cover load path.
Changed bore diameter, moved screw head/nut and service positions need current CAD interference/reuse/manufacturing identity checks before adoption. No such checks were run here.

limits: No actual PETG dimensions, stiffness, creep, tightening torque, bearing supply tolerances or axial force are known.
No value of screw preload or loss of lever running clearance is inferred from the .02 mismatch alone.
The current BOM correctly says M4x35 for this axis; the M4x30 premise was not used.
